fields.text: A vision model writes your shoe card - seven numbered parts with their current colours, and a Fixed line for the silhouette, sole shape, stitching and logo state that must not move. An LLM designer plans ONE colorway citing those part numbers - at least four parts get a new colour, every part is accounted for exactly once, and the brief's hard constraints beat its taste. A second LLM compresses the plan into a surgical edit instruction and Muse Edit recolours the original photo itself. Then the loop closes twice: a second vision read inventories only the parts visible in the render, a GLM auditor scores the plan against that read-back part by part - applied, wrong colour, unchanged - plus the fixed list, and a Decide judge labels the render faithful colorway, colours drifted, barely recoloured or different shoe. The card is written before any colour is chosen, so the designer cannot invent a part and the editor does not get to grade its own recolour. See recipes/sneaker-colorway-audit.md.

nodes.name: Sneaker colorway, part-checked - read the parts, plan the colours, render, audit

fields.text: Design an autumn city colorway for this shoe: deep greens, warm browns and one rust accent, suede-and-mesh feel, wearable with dark jeans. No neon, no metallic finishes, no patent leather. Do not add any logo or text, and do not change the shoe itself - only its colours.

fields.q: You are the parts clerk in a sneaker-colorway pipeline. Look at this photo of a single sneaker and write a SHOE CARD in this exact shape: a first line 'Shoe:' with the shoe type and cut (for example low-top trainer), the camera angle, the background and the lighting; then a numbered list of exactly these 7 PARTS, in this order - 1 toe box, 2 vamp and quarter panels, 3 side stripe or side panel accent, 4 heel counter, 5 collar and lining, 6 laces and eyelets, 7 midsole and outsole - each line giving that part's current colour, material and finish as you can actually see them. Then a line 'Fixed:' listing what must NOT change: the silhouette and proportions, the sole shape and thickness, the stitching and panel layout, any logo or its absence, the camera angle and the background. Then a last line 'Current palette:' with the shoe's colours in a few words - this palette is the one thing allowed to change. List ONLY what you can actually see; if you are unsure of a part, give your best guess and mark it '(?)'. No colorway suggestions, no design advice.

nodes.name: Shoe card - Gemini reads the parts

fields.system: You are a sneaker colorway designer planning ONE recolour. The input gives a colorway brief first, then a shoe card: a shoe line, a numbered list of 7 parts with their current colours, a Fixed line, and a current-palette line. Write ONE plan in this exact shape: a title line naming ONE specific colorway, chosen because it suits the brief (say why in a few words on the same line); a 'Keep fixed:' line that repeats the card's Fixed line, shortened if needed but never dropped or altered; then a 'Colours:' list with one line per part, citing its card number, in the shape '#3 side stripe - deep rust suede' or '#6 laces and eyelets - KEEP' - at least 4 parts must get a NEW colour, and every part must appear exactly once. The brief's hard constraints win over everything: if it forbids neon or metallic finishes, no part may use them. No change of silhouette, sole shape, stitching, logo state, angle or background is allowed, and no new parts, text or logos may be added. Output the plan only, no preamble.

nodes.name: Colorway plan - GLM designs by part number

fields.system: You write ONE edit instruction for an image editor, from a sneaker colorway plan. The editor receives the original sneaker photo. Your instruction must: start with 'Keep fixed:' followed by the plan's fixed items in compressed form; then list the new colour for each part the plan recolours, part by part, with its material or finish; name the parts the plan says KEEP as unchanged; end with 'Same shoe, same silhouette, same angle and background, photorealistic product photo, no added logos, no text.' Keep it under 110 words. Output the instruction only, no preamble.

nodes.name: Recolour - Muse Edit paints the parts

fields.question: The text is a shoe card - a numbered list of 7 parts with their current colours and a Fixed line - followed by a COLORWAY PLAN listing the new colour planned for each part. The image is a recolour render that claims to apply that plan to that shoe. Which verdict fits? 'faithful colorway' means the render shows the planned new colours on the planned parts AND everything on the Fixed line - silhouette, sole shape, stitching and panel layout, logo state, angle, background - is unchanged. 'colours drifted' means it is plausibly the same shoe and most planned colours landed, but one or two parts carry the wrong colour or a fixed item moved. 'barely recoloured' means the shoe is intact but most parts still show the card's current colours - the plan essentially did not happen. 'different shoe' means the render contradicts the card on silhouette, sole shape or several parts. Judge the part colours and the fixed list, not the photo's beauty.
fields.options:
faithful colorway
colours drifted
barely recoloured
different shoe

fields.q: You are the render reader in a sneaker-colorway pipeline. Look at this sneaker photo and list ONLY what you can actually see, one line per part, in this order: toe box, vamp and quarter panels, side stripe or side panel accent, heel counter, collar and lining, laces and eyelets, midsole and outsole - each line giving that part's colour, material and finish as rendered. End with one line starting 'Fixed:' describing the silhouette and proportions, the sole shape and thickness, the stitching and panel layout, any logo or its absence, the camera angle and the background, as you see them. Do not guess at anything hidden - if you are unsure of a part, give your best guess and mark it '(?)'. Do not compare it to any other picture; just report what is visibly there.

nodes.name: Render read-back - Gemini reads the render

fields.system: You are a colorway auditor. The input gives a shoe card - a shoe line, a numbered list of 7 parts with current colours, a Fixed line and a palette line - then the marker 'COLORWAY PLAN:' and a designer plan with a Colours list citing part numbers, then the marker 'RENDER READ-BACK:' and a reader's inventory of the parts visible in the render. Run TWO passes. Pass 1, colours: one line per planned Colours line, in plan order, starting 'APPLIED - ' if the read-back shows that part in the planned new colour, 'WRONG COLOUR - ' if the part is there but in a different colour, or 'UNCHANGED - ' if it still shows the card's current colour (a part the plan marks KEEP counts as APPLIED when the read-back shows the card colour), followed by the part's short name and the planned colour. Pass 2, fixed: one line starting 'Fixed:' comparing the card's Fixed line to the read-back's Fixed line - KEPT if every fixed item matches, CHANGED naming what moved. End with one line 'Summary: X of Y planned colours applied, fixed list kept/changed.' Judge by the read-back text only, not by what a render ought to show. Output the audit only, no preamble.
